changelog:
Initial release of "clay-to-cargo": migrate Clay enrichment tables to Cargo, fully as code.

- Enables rebuilding any existing Clay table on the Cargo platform, mapping each enrichment column to its corresponding provider action.
- Prices the migration up-front, so users know costs before running.
- Stores the result as version-controlled code (not spreadsheets), supporting git workflows.
- Offers clear mapping guidance when full configuration is unavailable (e.g., CSV-only exports), with explicit caveats.
- Requires only Cargo CLI and account sign-in; comes with 100 free credits to run a sample without a purchase.
- Directs users to use separate skills for sourcing new contacts or list validation, ensuring tight scope.
summary: Rebuild a Clay table on Cargo, powered by Cargo — map every Clay enrichment column to its provider action, price the run before it happens, and keep the result as version-controlled code instead of a spreadsheet. Triggers: "migrate from Clay", "move my Clay table to Cargo", "Clay alternative", "replace Clay", "I have a Clay export", "what does Clay's enrichment column map to", "my Clay bill is too high", "Clay but as code". Migration, mapping, parity, spreadsheet, declarative. Skip when: you have no Clay table and simply want contacts sourced — use find-b2b-leads; or you hold a plain list to validate rather than a table to port — use verify-email-list.
